comment: E5 Round 27 — late-arriving Anchor idempotency. Spec authority: federation/move-anchor-replication.md. Peer B sees a Move m1 directly from peer A (e.g. via push). Later, peer A's Anchor for m1 arrives at peer B (e.g. via pull). Applying the Anchor must NOT double-effect — m1 was already projected; the Anchor only finalizes ordering metadata. Idempotency is the load-bearing invariant.

encoder.anchor_apply_rule: if all moves in the anchor are already projected on this peer, anchor application is a metadata-only update (mark as anchored, no projection delta)

vectors.name: anchor_arrives_after_direct_move_idempotent
vectors.comment: Peer B receives Move m1 from peer A directly (via push). Peer B projects m1. Later, peer B pulls peer A's Anchor that includes m1 in its frontier. The anchor application MUST NOT re-project m1 — message_count stays 1, not 2.

expected.rationale: Anchor application is metadata-only when the move was already projected. No double-effect.

vectors.name: anchor_arrives_with_new_move_projects_once
vectors.comment: Anchor covers two moves: m1 (already projected) and m2 (new). The application projects m2 only — m1 is no-op.

expected.rationale: Mixed anchor: only the genuinely new move projects; the already-projected move is metadata-only.

vectors.name: duplicate_anchor_application_no_double_effect
vectors.comment: Peer B applies the same anchor twice. Second application is a complete no-op.

expected.rationale: Re-applying an already-applied anchor is a complete no-op.
